newsitem.title: FRANCE: Promodes sells German unit to Spar.
newsitem.headline: Promodes sells German unit to Spar.

text.p: French retailer Promodes announced on Monday it had reached an agreement to sell its German unit Promohypermarkt to Spar Handels AG.
"This agremeent will take effect on October 1, 1996," Promodes said in a statement, adding that the deal was subject to regulatory approval.
Promohypermarkt, bought by Promodes in 1990, has 36 stores trading under the Continent banner and lost 43 million marks last year, a spokesman said.
The spokesman would not disclose the sale price.
He said the 1996 accounts would reflect Promohypermarkt's losses to date. The disposal would start having a positive impact on Promodes' operating profit as of 1997, he said.
"This agreement allows us to exit honourably from Germany," he said. "It's the best solution."
The agreement will allow Spar, whose 1995 sales totalled 46.7 billion francs to increase its retail Interspar network that currently totals 49 stores, Promodes said.
Promodes, which sold Spar four stores last year, said the sale was part of its drive to "refocus and consolidate" its activities.
Talk of sale of the German unit pushed up Promodes shares on the Paris bourse last month.
The Promodes spokesman said the Promohypermarkt chain had been penalised by the fact it ranked 21st in size among German retailers.
"To succeed you really need to be among the top ones," he said.
Spar is currently eighth in size among German retailers. The acquisition "will make it one of the biggest chains in Germany" and give it more market clout, the Promodes spokesman said.
